FindingKindWire.description: Which kind of discrepancy this is; pick the one that fits best. action_without_result: an action was taken but no outcome for it was ever recorded; agent_criterion_unmet: a probe the agent itself chose beyond the task's stated scope fails: the agent's own criterion, which it may fix or narrow with a reason, never a task requirement; claim_without_admissible_evidence: readable claim and evidence records establish missing support; omitted source content or an already recorded capture gap alone makes content unassessable, not a new defect; code_defect: a concrete defect in the code shown in the packet prevents the requested behavior; completion_with_open_obligations: work is presented as finished while work obligations it was meant to satisfy remain open; an obligation only to obtain this review or run a FinishUP check is not one, but one to build, test, lint, or type-check the work is; contradictory_claims_unresolved: two claims in the packet cannot both be true and neither has been withdrawn or reconciled; decision_needed: a reasoned trade-off or conflicting task/input interpretations: present both with evidence and one discriminating check; advisory priority 3, never blocks closure; you decide and record the choice with respond; diff_does_not_match_account: the described change and the change actually shown in the packet differ in substance; evidence_does_not_support_claim: evidence is cited for a claim but does not establish what the claim asserts; failed_work_omitted: a recorded failure, error, or abandoned attempt is missing from the account given; ledger_stale_or_incomplete: the record of the work is behind or missing entries, so the packet cannot settle the question; FinishUP coverage levels and packet limit codes are not this; material_limitation_omitted: a limitation that changes how the result should be read was not disclosed; questionable_finding_rejection: a deterministic finding was dismissed or explained away without adequate grounds; requested_item_never_attempted: something the user or an obligation asked for was never worked on at all; result_without_action: an outcome is recorded with no action in the packet that produced it; stale_evidence_for_changed_state: the cited evidence predates a change to what it describes, so it no longer speaks to it; task_requirement_unmet: a requirement stated in the packet is not satisfied by the work shown; weak_or_stale_response: the answer given is thin or out of date relative to what the packet supports.

MissingForAssessmentKindWire.description: What kind of material you needed. command_identity: which command produced an output the packet shows; current_diff_for_path: the current change to a file the packet shows only in part or stale; other: anything else, named in the reason; plan_or_claim_text: the full text of a plan or claim the packet shows clipped; prior_finding_context: an earlier finding or the agent's answer to it; task_statement: what the user asked for; verification_output: the output of a test, build or lint run that a claim relies on.

PriorFindingVerdictWire.description: Your ruling on that finding alone. fixed: cited material recorded after the finding shows the problem is gone; still_present: newer material shows it remains; answered_not_fixed: the main agent answered but the problem remains, shown by material newer than its answer (without it FinishUP records a standing disagreement, not a round); withdrawn: you accept the main agent's rejection, or a limitation it acknowledged; unassessable: the packet cannot settle it, including when only an artifact the agent cannot obtain would settle it (never still_present then).

alternative_interpretation.description: The strongest honest reading under which there is no problem here. Write the case against your own challenge, not a weak version of it.

cited_refs.description: The refs this challenge rests on. Every value must appear in the packet's citable_refs array; an items[].item_id is not a ref. A value outside it is dropped, and a challenge left with no citable ref cannot become a finding, so cite the specific claim, obligation, event, or finding the discrepancy is about.

discrepancy.description: What the packet shows that does not fit, stated as fact rather than suspicion.

message_to_main_agent.description: What you are telling the agent, addressed to it directly: what you checked, what does not hold, and the repair or the exact missing artifact that would resolve it. Ask only for what the agent can produce from the task, the workspace, and the tools in the packet; never for a hidden grader, private specification, or less delivered work.

restates.description: When this challenge raises again the same problem, of the same finding_kind, as an earlier finding, that finding's finding_ref from review_packet.prior_finding_refs or a yoetz.settled-finding/1 row; otherwise null. The challenge is then recorded on that earlier finding instead of becoming a new finding.

snippet.description: One exact short quote copied verbatim from a provider-bound packet item that supports this challenge; never invent or paraphrase it.

summary.description: One short line naming the discrepancy, readable on its own.

uncertainty.description: What you could not determine from the packet and what would settle it. Say so plainly rather than hedging the challenge itself. If only an artifact the agent cannot obtain would settle it, the next step is state_unresolved_limitation.

reason.description: One short line saying why the packet could not be assessed without it.

target_refs.description: The packet refs this item concerns, only from citable_refs; empty when none applies. Never name a path, command or ref the packet does not contain.

cited_refs.description: The refs the ruling rests on, from citable_refs. fixed must cite evidence or a result recorded after the finding, or it is treated as unassessable.

finding_id.description: The earlier finding this ruling is about: one finding_ref from review_packet.prior_finding_refs. Give each listed finding exactly one ruling.

note.description: One short sentence saying why, addressed to the main agent.

cited_refs.description: The packet refs supporting this judgement, each from citable_refs; never cite an items[].item_id.

requirement_or_claim.description: The requirement or claim being assessed, stated as a short packet-grounded label.

snippet.description: One exact short quote copied verbatim from a provider-bound packet item; required for supported or not_supported, and null for not_assessable.

ReviewerFileAction.description: Read lines of a file, or list a directory, beneath a root_id from the packet's catalog.

ReviewerLedgerAction.description: Read up to 8 recorded task records linked to up to 4 refs.

ReviewerNextStepWire.description: The single kind of response you are asking the agent for. act: do the missing work; provide_evidence: record a named artifact that already exists but is not in the packet, never a re-run of verification whose output the packet already carries; revise_claim: correct or withdraw what was claimed; dispute_with_evidence: rebut this challenge if you believe it is wrong; state_unresolved_limitation: disclose what remains after a recorded concrete resolution attempt, or name the specific authority or environment blocker preventing that attempt, or the artifact the agent cannot obtain that alone would settle it (never request act or provide_evidence for such an artifact; the agent settles this request by acknowledging it once, so ask for nothing else beside it); answer_question: you need the agent's answer before you can judge (an interpretation it chose, a check it may have run); put the question in discrepancy, and the next review reads the answer.

ReviewerPacketAction.description: Read one packet item from a byte offset, including what the packet cut. Bytes FinishUP never kept are not_retained.

VerifiedVerdictWire.description: supported: the packet supports it; not_supported: the packet contradicts or lacks it; not_assessable: the packet does not carry enough material to judge.
